TelemetryData.title: TelemetryData
TelemetryData.description: Represents anonymous telemetry data captured from website traffic.

id.description: Unique identifier for the telemetry data record.

timestamp.description: Timestamp of when the telemetry data was recorded.

pageView.description: The URL or route of the page visited.

userAgent.description: User agent string of the browser used.

ipAddress.description: IP address of the user (anonymized for privacy).

deviceType.description: Type of device used (e.g., desktop, mobile, tablet).

operatingSystem.description: Operating system used (e.g., Windows, macOS, iOS, Android).

location.description: Geographic location based on IP address (coarse-grained).

ContactFormSubmission.title: ContactFormSubmission
ContactFormSubmission.description: Represents data submitted through the contact form.

id.description: Unique identifier for the contact form submission.

submissionDate.description: Date and time the form was submitted.

name.description: Name of the person submitting the form.

email.description: Email address of the person submitting the form.

message.description: The message content from the contact form.

DriverApplication.title: DriverApplication
DriverApplication.description: Represents a driver application submitted through the driver recruitment page.

id.description: Unique identifier for the driver application.

applicationDate.description: Date and time the application was submitted.

firestore.reasoning:
Given the requirement to view results directly in Firebase and the nature of the entities (telemetry data, contact form submissions, driver applications), a flat collection structure is suitable. This simplifies querying and avoids unnecessary complexity for the relatively simple data relationships. Authorization independence isn't a major concern here as these are mostly data capture scenarios where access control is minimal (likely only write access with potential review access for admins). However, if access controls become more granular in the future, denormalization of authorization data will be required.

The solution segregates the different types of data into separate collections (`telemetry_data`, `contact_form_submissions`, `driver_applications`) to maintain a homogeneous security posture. This segregation ensures that rules can be applied consistently to all documents within each collection.

Since all the collections are designed to capture information (telemetry, applications and submissions), no extra roles or authorization is required besides the write rules. Thus, this design avoids authorization dependencies and supports basic QAPs by segregating data types into dedicated collections.
